## Question 3 (6 points)

A small bakery wants to estimate the average weight of a batch of its croissants. The croissant weights are normally distributed, but since the population standard deviation is unknown, they collect a random sample of 12 croissants and measure their weights (in grams). The observations can be found below.

First, Construct a 90% confidence interval for the true mean weight of the croissants without using the `t.test` function. Then construct a 90% confidence interval using the `t.test` function and compare the two intervals to make sure they match.

```{r, echo = TRUE}
weights <- c(51.62, 57.53, 55.50, 50.94, 48.12, 55.08, 48.08, 44.25, 45.79, 53.67, 46.13, 55.13)

```

## Question 4 (5 points)

A large manufacturing company produces light bulbs and wants to estimate the average lifespan of a particular model. The lifespans are not normally distributed. The company knows from historical data that the standard deviation of bulb lifespans is 100 hours. A random sample of 50 bulbs is tested. These observations can be found below. Construct a 95% confidence interval for the true mean lifespan of these bulbs.
